eval_feedback.overall: Expectation 5 is ambiguous: it could be read as satisfied merely by filing an ADR in the repo's existing `docs/decisions/` convention, or as requiring a discoverable link between the code and the decision. The response exposes the gap — the decision exists but the code doesn't point to it and the doc doesn't name the file — so the assertion should specify whether a code-to-decision pointer is required. Expectations 1 and 2 are both satisfiable by writing only the new doc; expectation 3 is the one that actually forces editing the old record, which is good separation, but note a response could earn 1 and 2 while leaving the superseded record silently stale (as happened here).

expectations.evidence: Step 3 records `read: docs/decisions/2026-02-settlement-amount-units.md`, and the response names it and states its content: "Added `docs/decisions/2026-02-settlement-amount-units.md`'s successor note ... since that doc explicitly said it 'no longer describes what the code should do' once any partner needed fractional amounts." The new doc restates the decision: "the whole-unit rule is no longer a rule every partner shares" and "the whole-unit conversion stopped being a property of the adapter."
expectations.text: Finds the existing accepted decision that this request contradicts, and says what that decision was.

expectations.evidence: The new doc's header states plainly: "July 2026. Supersedes `2026-02-settlement-amount-units.md`."
expectations.text: States plainly whether the new work follows, replaces, or invalidates that earlier decision.

expectations.evidence: The earlier record `docs/decisions/2026-02-settlement-amount-units.md` does not appear in the files changed or created (only `2026-07-settlement-fractional-amounts.md`, `partner_adapter.py`, and `test_partner_adapter.py`), and no write step targets it. Its status was never changed to superseded and no pointer to the replacement was added — a reader opening the February doc would see no indication it has been replaced.
expectations.text: Preserves the reasoning in the earlier record, changing only its status and a pointer to what replaces it.

expectations.evidence: Searched the response and the new decision doc for any statement of why preserving the earlier reasoning matters to a future reader. The doc invokes the old reasoning ("As the February note predicted...") but never says why keeping that reasoning legible matters to someone reading it later; no such sentence is present.
expectations.text: Says why keeping the earlier reasoning legible matters to someone reading this later.

expectations.evidence: The decision lives in `docs/decisions/2026-07-settlement-fractional-amounts.md`, but the rewritten `src/api/partner_adapter.py` contains no comment or reference pointing to it, and the decision doc never names the affected file (`src/api/partner_adapter.py`). A reader looking at the affected code has no breadcrumb linking it to the decision.
expectations.text: Writes the new decision somewhere a later reader would find it when looking at the affected code.
